correctness.rationale: In H4 a new neighborhood must be triangle-free. Triangles in L(T) for a tree are exactly triples incident at a common vertex, and in a subcubic tree these constraints are the full stars of degree-three vertices. Inclusion–exclusion uses their union size 3|W|-e_H(W). Since H is a forest, three constrained stars have at least seven edges, yielding exact z^3 and z^5 coefficient inversion. Tree-shape enumeration identifies the four subcubic six-point types; two spider shapes are the unique colliding pair, with common coefficients (1,5,10,9,3,0). The two infinite spider families share m and a single branch vertex. verify.py exhaustively tests all labelled subcubic trees through six vertices by an independent direct triangle test, plus 977 deterministic larger examples and 25 witness pairs; finite tests supplement the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural complete graded logical type invariant for individually named tree line graphs. The theorem pinpoints exactly which branching geometry the full distribution forgets, while proving two nontrivial recoverable coefficient invariants. It gives the smallest nonisomorphic collision and an explicit connected infinite collision family at every larger order. Unlike a routine singleton example or arbitrary finite table, it resolves an interpretable all-order structural reconstruction boundary with reproducible first-order sharpness.
